categories.label: Bioinformatics portal
categories.comment: web site providing a platform/portal to multiple resources used for research in a focused area, including biological databases, web applications, training resources and so on.

categories.label: Command-line tool
categories.comment: A tool with a text-based (command-line) interface.

categories.label: Database portal
categories.comment: A Web application, suite or workbench providing a portal to a biological database.

categories.label: Desktop application
categories.comment: A tool with a graphical user interface that runs on your desktop environment, e.g. on a PC or mobile device.

categories.label: Helpdesk
categories.comment: A service providing assistance with the use of bioinformatics tools, data resources, or any other aspect of bioinformatics.

categories.label: Library
categories.comment: A collection of components that are used to construct other tools. bio.tools scope includes component libraries performing high-level bioinformatics functions but excludes lower-level programming libraries.

categories.label: Ontology
categories.comment: A collection of information about concepts, including terms, synonyms, descriptions etc.

categories.label: Plug-in
categories.comment: A software component encapsulating a set of related functions, which are not standalone, i.e. depend upon other software for its use, e.g. a Javascript widget, or a plug-in, extension add-on etc. that extends the function of some existing tool.

categories.label: SPARQL endpoint
categories.comment: A service that provides queries over an RDF knowledge base via the SPARQL query language and protocol, and returns results via HTTP.

categories.label: Script
categories.comment: A tool written for some run-time environment (e.g. other applications or an OS shell) that automates the execution of tasks. Often a small program written in a general-purpose languages (e.g. Perl, Python) or some domain-specific languages (e.g. sed).

categories.label: Suite
categories.comment: A collection of tools which are bundled together into a convenient toolkit. Such tools typically share related functionality, a common user interface and can exchange data conveniently. This includes collections of stand-alone command-line tools, or Web applications within a common portal.

categories.label: Web API
categories.comment: An application programming interface (API) consisting of endpoints to a request-response message system accessible via HTTP. Includes everything from simple data-access URLs to RESTful APIs.

categories.label: Web application
categories.comment: A tool with a graphical user interface that runs in your Web browser.

categories.label: Web service
categories.comment: An API described in a machine readable form (typically WSDL) providing programmatic access via SOAP over HTTP.

categories.label: Workbench
categories.comment: An application or suite with a graphical user interface, providing an integrated environment for data analysis which includes or may be extended with any number of functions or tools. Includes workflow systems, platforms, frameworks etc.

categories.label: Workflow
categories.comment: A set of tools which have been composed together into a pipeline of some sort. Such tools are (typically) standalone, but are composed for convenience, for instance for batch execution via some workflow engine or script.
